meta.unit: Malachi given to the record (3 Nephi 24–25)
principles: A burning day and a healing one held together
An old law told to be remembered
A promise about fathers and children

world_behind.title: The frame is in the previous chapter
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 24:1 gave the attribution and this chapter runs on without a new introduction.

world_behind.title: It is Malachi 4 in full
world_behind.text: All six verses correspond to the six of Malachi 4.

world_behind.title: One word carries the largest difference
world_behind.text: Verse 2 reads "Son of Righteousness" where Malachi 4:2 reads "Sun of righteousness".

world_behind.title: A second change is a preposition
world_behind.text: Verse 2 has calves "in the stall" where Malachi 4:2 has calves "of the stall".

world_behind.title: The rest matches closely
world_behind.text: Verses 1, 3, 4, 5, and 6 differ from Malachi 4 only in punctuation and capitalization.

world_behind.title: The law of Moses is told to be remembered
world_behind.text: Verse 4 says this in a chapter given after 3 Nephi 15:5 declared the law fulfilled.

world_behind.title: The explanation comes after
world_behind.text: 3 Nephi 26:1 says he expounded these things once the quotation was finished.

words.text: A closed chamber for baking or firing. The record uses the word twice, here and at 3 Nephi 13:30, and the King James Bible twelve times. Verse 1 uses it for how the day burns.
The stalks left standing after a harvest. Treated at 2 Nephi 26:4. It appears six times in the record, and the King James Bible eighteen.
The limbs a bird flies with, and by extension shelter. The record uses the word eight times and the King James Bible seventy-six. Verse 2 puts healing in them.
A stable compartment where an animal is kept and fed. The word turns up twice, here and again at 1 Nephi 22:24, here, and the King James Bible three times. Verse 2 has calves growing up in it.
The undersides of the feet. The record uses the word once, here, and the King James Bible seven times. Verse 3 has the wicked as ashes beneath them.
The mountain where the law was given, called Sinai elsewhere. The record uses the name once, here, and the King James Bible seventeen times. Verse 4 names it as the place of the commandment.
The prophet of the northern kingdom, taken up without dying. One use of the name here against sixty-nine in the King James Bible. Verse 5 says he will be sent before the great day.

phrases.term: The day cometh that shall burn as an oven
phrases.text: The image that opens the chapter. Verse 1 says the same day burns the proud and those who do wickedly.

phrases.term: It shall leave them neither root nor branch
phrases.text: Destruction described in two directions. Nothing below ground and nothing above it survives.

phrases.term: Unto you that fear my name
phrases.text: The turn in the chapter. The same day that burns is described for a second group in the next clause.
Malachi 4:2 has "Sun of righteousness". The change names a person where the older text has a figure of light.

phrases.term: Arise with healing in his wings
phrases.text: Rising and healing in one motion. The image keeps the flight of the older reading while the subject changes.

phrases.term: Grow up as calves in the stall
phrases.text: Malachi 4:2 has calves "of the stall". The preposition puts the animals inside the shelter rather than describing where they came from.

phrases.term: They shall be ashes under the soles of your feet
phrases.text: The end of the burning image from verse 1. What was stubble is now underfoot.

phrases.term: Remember ye the law of Moses, my servant
phrases.text: An instruction to remember a law 3 Nephi 15:5 had said was fulfilled. The remembering and the ending stand in the same book.

phrases.term: Which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel
phrases.text: The law placed at a specific mountain and given to a whole nation. The verse names where and for whom.

phrases.term: The great and dreadful day of the Lord
phrases.text: One day with two adjectives. Verse 1 and verse 2 had already shown both sides of it.

phrases.term: He shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children
phrases.text: The last verse of the quotation. It matches Malachi 4:6 word for word.

verses.label: v. 1–6
verses.title: The least altered chapter in the volume
verses.text: Twenty-four chapters here quote a King James chapter at length. This one changes one verse of six, and the whole of the change is two words in verse 2. Verses 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 stand word for word as the King James prints them. Only 2 Nephi 22 matches it, at one verse of six; the next lightest, 2 Nephi 21, changes nearly twice as large a share. Whatever governed the handling of quoted material was not applied here at all.

verses.label: v. 1
verses.title: A phrase that occurs once
verses.text: The chapter opens on the oven and the stubble and ends the verse with "neither root nor branch," a figure for leaving no remainder of a family. Those three words appear in this verse and nowhere else in the whole volume. Nothing in the verse is altered, and the chapter's most striking image is therefore one it did not supply and did not touch.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: One letter
verses.text: The King James verse promises "the Sun of righteousness" rising with healing in his wings, an image of daybreak. Here it is "the Son of Righteousness." The change is a single letter, and it does not stand alone: "Son of Righteousness" is what this volume calls him at 2 Ne. 26:9 and again at Ether 9:22, while "Sun of righteousness" occurs nowhere in it. Two of those three uses come long before Malachi lived, so the quotation is being brought into line with a title the book had already settled on rather than the other way about.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: Of the stall, or in it
verses.text: The second word to change in the chapter is a preposition. Malachi's calves grow up "of the stall" and here they grow up "in the stall." The volume itself uses the King James form: Nephi writes that the righteous "must be led up as calves of the stall" at 1 Ne. 22:24, six centuries earlier in the story and in his own prose rather than inside a quoted block. So the book holds both readings, and the one that departs from the King James text falls in the one place where the King James text is being copied.

verses.label: v. 4
verses.title: A command left standing
verses.text: Verse 4 is reproduced exactly: "Remember ye the law of Moses, my servant, which I commanded unto him in Horeb for all Israel, with the statutes and judgments." It is the only imperative in the chapter, and it is read aloud to people who have been told ten chapters earlier that "the law is fulfilled that was given unto Moses" (3 Ne. 15:4) and that "the law which was given unto Moses hath an end in me" (3 Ne. 15:8). Nothing here softens or qualifies the command, and no explanation is offered for reading it to them.

verses.label: v. 5–6
verses.title: Malachi's singular, not Luke's plural
verses.text: The closing promise about Elijah is untouched, including a detail that separates two versions of it. Malachi 4:6 turns "the heart of the fathers to the children," and the angel in Luke 1:17 turns "the hearts of the fathers to the children." This chapter follows Malachi and keeps the singular in both halves of the verse. The volume knows the plural form, since Luke's phrasing is the one in wide circulation, and it is not the one used here.

chapter.title: Six verses hold two opposite futures
chapter.text: Verse 1 burns and verse 2 heals. The chapter puts them on the same day.

chapter.title: A single letter changes the reading
chapter.text: Verse 2 has Son where Malachi 4:2 has Sun. The figure of the rising light becomes a person.

chapter.title: The animals are sheltered rather than sourced
chapter.text: Verse 2 has calves in the stall. Malachi 4:2 describes them as calves of it.

chapter.title: The law is kept in view after being fulfilled
chapter.text: Verse 4 says remember it. 3 Nephi 15:5 had already said it has an end in him.

chapter.title: The location of the giving is named
chapter.text: Verse 4 says Horeb and says it was for all Israel. The instruction to remember comes with its address.

chapter.title: The last promise is domestic
chapter.text: Verse 6 is about parents and children. The chapter of fire closes on a household.

chapter.title: The curse is what turning prevents
chapter.text: Verse 6 gives the alternative in its final clause. The consequence is stated rather than implied.

chapter.title: Nothing here is explained on the page
chapter.text: 3 Nephi 26:1 says the expounding happened after. The chapter is quotation only.

applications.title: Read the same day from both sides
applications.text: The day that burns is the day that heals. What it is depends on where you are standing.

applications.title: Notice the small word
applications.text: Son for Sun, and in for of. Two changes of a letter or a preposition carry the chapter's differences.

applications.title: The reversal is stated as complete
applications.text: Those who were set up become ashes under the soles of the feet of the people they had trodden on. When a picture of justice is offered, notice whether it merely stops the harm or actually turns the positions around.

applications.title: Keep remembering what has been fulfilled
applications.text: The law was told to be remembered after it ended in him. Fulfilment is not a reason to stop reading.

applications.title: The warning arrives with a preparation attached
applications.text: Elijah is sent before the great and dreadful day, so the announcement and the provision for it occupy the same sentence. Hard news in this book usually carries an instruction alongside it.

applications.title: Turn toward your parents and your children
applications.text: The last verse makes that the work Elijah comes for. It is stated as the thing that keeps the earth from a curse.

questions.text: What in my life is stubble?
What would healing in his wings mean for me this year?
Whose defeat am I looking forward to more than I should?
Which older commandment have I stopped remembering?
What am I expecting to be sent before I am ready?
Which way is my heart turned, toward my fathers or away?
What has my turning cost, and what has it saved?
